 Order

The petitioner is the 2nd accused in C.C. No.200/2017 on the file of the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, Ernakulam, which has arisen from Crime No.2158/2016 registered by the Ernakulam Central Police Station alleging the offences punishable under Sections 406, 420 and 506(1) read with 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

2. The learned counsel for the petitioner and the learned counsel appearing for the 2 nd respondent jointly submit that the dispute that led to the registration of the crime has been amicably settled between the parties before the High Court Mediation Centre, Ernakulam, as per the terms and conditions in the memorandum of settlement agreement dated 30.06.2025 2025:KER:85015 Crl.MC No. 3688 OF 2025 signed by the parties and counter signed by the respective counsel.
The learned counsel for the 2nd respondent submits that, the petitioner has already paid Rs.50,00,000/- to the 2nd respondent as agreed in the agreement.
Therefore, the 2nd respondent has no objection in all further proceedings in C.C. No.200/2017 being quashed.

3. The scope and ambit of the inherent powers of this Court to quash criminal proceedings on the ground of settlement between the parties have been authoritatively laid down by Hon'ble Supreme Court, in Gian Singh v. State of Punjab [(2012) 10 SCC 303], State of Madhya Pradesh v. Laxmi Narayan and Others [(2019) 5 SCC 688], Naushey Ali v. State of U.P. [(2025) 4 SCC 78], and in a Girish Menon vs State Of Kerala on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/128258535/
2 host of judicial pronouncements.

sentences.text:
It is held that in cases where the offences are not grave or heinous,
and where the parties have amicably settled the dispute, to secure the ends of justice, the High Court may invoke its 2025:KER:85015 Crl.MC No. 3688 OF 2025 inherent powers to quash the proceedings, particularly if continuation of the prosecution would serve no fruitful purpose.

4. On an overall consideration of the facts and circumstances of the present case, and the materials on record, I am satisfied that: the offences alleged are not heinous or of a serious nature; no public interest or element of societal concern is involved; the chances of conviction are remote in view of the settlement; and the continuation of the proceedings would merely burden the judicial process without advancing the cause of justice.
Furthermore, the settlement would promote harmony between the parties and restore peace.
Hence, this Court is persuaded to hold that this is a fit case to exercise its inherent jurisdiction.
In the result, this Crl.M.C. is allowed.

Accordingly, Annexure-A1 Final Report in C.C. No.
No.200/2017 on the file of the Court of the Chief Judicial Magistrate, 2025:KER:85015 Crl.MC No.
3688 OF 2025 Ernakulam, as against the accused persons are hereby quashed.
